documents.title: AI Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page offers a 'framework and guidance for the responsible and ethical use of AI' and sends users to role-specific guidelines. Its prohibitions are general-conduct ones (privacy, security, 'Academic Integrity Violations') and it names no default rule for coursework, so it sets no stance itself.
documents.summary: The university hub page for Mason's AI guidelines. It gives role-based entry points, a definition of generative AI, guiding principles (oversight, transparency, data security, privacy, critical thinking, accuracy, accessibility) and a list of AI uses that violate standing university policies. It sets no course-level stance on AI use.

documents.stance_why: The page states 'Decisions about individual course-level policies should remain the sole responsibility of course instructors' and that 'it is possible to have very different rules and guidelines about AI use in different classes', so the university delegates while offering student advice.
documents.summary: Student-facing university guidance. It frames AI use around critical literacy and learning, tells students to follow each course's syllabus or ask the instructor, asks them to acknowledge AI use, warns about detectors, privacy and copyright, and lists beneficial and discouraged uses. Course-level decisions are left to instructors.
